data.name: Octavien
data.long_meaning: Derived from Octavius, the name Octavien means 'Seventh, eighth, or eighth man'. The name gained popularity through Octavian, the adopted name of Gaius Octavius Thurinus, who later became Caesar Augustus, the first Roman emperor. This name holds a rich history and is deeply rooted in the Christian tradition.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name inspired by the strength and leadership of the Roman emperor Octavian, symbolizing devotion, resilience, and determination.

in_hebrew.name: אוקטאווין
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אוקטאווין הוא שם שמקורו ברומי, ומשמעותו 'השמיני' או 'נולד אחרי שבעה'. השם קשור למספר שמונה, שמסמל התחלה חדשה ושלמות. במסורת הנוצרית, השם אוקטאווין עשוי להיות קשור לנושא של תחילתה של תקופה חדשה ושלמה יותר.

in_greek.name: Οκταβίων
in_greek.long_meaning: Οκταβίων είναι ένα όνομα Ρωμαϊκής προέλευσης, που σημαίνει 'ο όγδοος' ή 'γεννημένος μετά επτά'. Το όνομα συνδέεται με τον αριθμό οκτώ, που συμβολίζει μια νέα αρχή και πληρότητα. Στην Χριστιανική παράδοση, το όνομα Οκταβίων μπορεί να συνδέεται με το θέμα της έναρξης μιας νέας και πληρέστερης περιόδου.

historical_references.reference: Octavian was the adopted name of Gaius Octavius Thurinus, born in 63 BC in Velitrae, Italy. He rose to power through political maneuvering and military campaigns, becoming the first Roman emperor in 27 BC at the age of 31.
historical_references.context: Octavian, also known as Octavianus or Octavianus Augustus, was the founding father of the Roman Empire. He was the great-nephew of Julius Caesar and adopted his name following Caesar's assassination in 44 BC.

historical_references.reference: Octavian assumed the title 'Christian Emperor' in the 4th century AD, during the period of Late Antiquity when Christianity became the dominant religion in the Roman Empire. This title did not signify a religious conversion, but rather a recognition of the importance of Christianity in the empire's political structure.
historical_references.context: Octavian's Christian name is a later development, unrelated to his original Roman name. It is a testament to the changing religious and political landscape of the Roman Empire during Late Antiquity.
